summary: Bradford's parks and environment record spans neighbourhood recreation, waterfront and beach management, urban forestry, ravine protection, climate action, and EV infrastructure. Bradford opposes closing recreation facilities such as Weston Arena and rinks, and advocates expanding capacity through new pickleball courts, cricket pitches, splash pads, and disc golf. Bradford presses the City on service delivery basics: open pools during heat waves, functioning washrooms, clean parks, and garbage collection. Bradford supports EV charging expansion, district energy, TransformTO net zero goals, ravine restoration (Small's Creek, Taylor Creek), tree planting, and a single-use plastics ban. Bradford opposes encampments in parks and playgrounds. Bradford opposed the toboggan ban and moved to reverse it. Bradford has criticized the current mayor's Parks budget increase and tree equity policy, arguing accountability should precede added hiring.

key_positions.stance: Opposes closing municipal recreation facilities such as Weston Arena and other rinks; supports investing in net new recreation instead of cannibalizing existing facilities.
Supports expanding accessible recreation options, including dedicated pickleball courts, cricket pitches, splash pads, skateparks, and disc golf.
Supports keeping pools, park washrooms, and other basic amenities open and functioning, particularly during heat waves and summer weekends.
Supports Toronto's climate goals, including net zero by 2040, TransformTO, EV charging expansion, and district energy adoption.
Supports protecting ravines and the tree canopy, including Small's Creek advocacy and community tree planting.
Opposes tent encampments in parks and playgrounds and supports clearing them while connecting people to supports.
Opposes Toronto's ban on tobogganing at 45 hills and supports common-sense safety mitigation instead.
Supports the Alcohol in Parks pilot allowing responsible outdoor drinking.
Supports restricting motorized watercraft (jet skis) at Woodbine Beach while keeping paddleboards and kayaks welcome.
Opposes the current Parks budget approach of adding staff without accountability, and opposes the tree equity policy as a distraction from core priorities.
Supports banning single-use plastics in Toronto.
